note.after_visit_summary: You came in for rough spots on the top of your head. We found six rough, scaly spots from years of sun. These are called actinic keratoses, which are precancerous but usually never turn into cancer. We treated all six today by freezing them with liquid nitrogen. Over the next few days they will get red, maybe blister, then crust and peel off in 1 to 3 weeks. You can put a little petroleum jelly on them. If any spot has not healed in 6 weeks or starts growing, please come back so we can take a small sample. You should use sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher every morning on your scalp, face, ears, and the backs of your hands, and reapply every 2 hours when you are outside. A wide-brimmed hat that covers your ears and neck and long sleeves will help too. We will see you again in 6 months for a full skin check. Other spots on your back are harmless skin tags and do not need treatment.
